text:
eli: quick question — saw a customer trace where the runtime does a prefetch of KV entries before streaming. In our usage payload, should those prefetch tokens show up as prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, or neither?

nina: can you paste the call and the usage blob?

eli: sure — simplified: 
```
POST /v1/generate?stream=true
body: { model: "redwood-llm-xl", prompt: "summarize:", context_prefetch: true }
response.usage: { prompt_tokens: 45, completion_tokens: 120, cached_tokens: 30 }
```
logs show prefetch happened before streaming started. The ambiguity: those 30 cached_tokens appear in the same usage object as the prompt. Are we confident they should be *cached* (non-billable) even if they were materialized into the request flow prior to first streamed chunk?

ramon: short answer: they should be cached/non-billable if origin == "kv_prefetch" and we didn't re-synthesize them. We have two failure modes: (1) materialized from local cache -> cached, (2) re-tokenized or regenerated -> billable. We need an explicit origin tag to avoid ad-hoc rules.

devex: +1 on origin tag. Backwards-compat note: older SDKs expect flat usage fields. We should add an optional `usage.cached_origin` array and a tiny `usage.flags` map rather than repurposing prompt_tokens. That way no change in existing semantics.

accounting-bot: auto-note: reconciliation job (last 24h) shows ~0.4% divergence on customers with heavy prefetch. Root cause likely attribution ambiguity like this.

eli: proposed schema snippet: 
```
usage: {
  prompt_tokens: 45,
  completion_tokens: 120,
  cached_tokens: 30,
  cached_origin: ["kv_prefetch"],
  flags: { streaming_prefetch: true }
}
```
This keeps old fields but adds a small signal. Does that satisfy accounting and SDK compatibility?

ramon: yes, that would let accounting ignore cached_tokens unless cached_origin is empty/unknown. Also need a rule for streaming partial flushes: if prefetch is streamed in the first chunk, don't double-count it as billed completion tokens later. We should emit `usage.stream_prefetch_bytes` or a boolean `flags.streamed_prefetch` so reconcilers don't double-count.

nina: devex, will this require changes to the Node/py SDKs? If so, can we make the SDKs tolerate missing `cached_origin` gracefully?

devex: SDK change plan: (1) parse `usage.cached_origin` if present and attach to Usage object, (2) treat unknown extra fields as opaque in all SDK versions. No breaking changes. I'll add tests for streaming prefetch scenarios.

eli: workflow ask — i'll open a tiny RFC + runtime PR to surface origin at the usage emission point and add the `flags.streaming_prefetch` boolean. Ramon's reconciliation rules go in accounting playbook.

ramon: sounds good. One more edge: what about model-side context window prefetch (model priors) vs customer-side cached prefixes? We need distinct origins like `model_prefill` vs `kv_prefetch`. Add both to `cached_origin` enum.

accounting-bot: noted (automated): recon job scheduled with new heuristics once fields land.

infra-bot: deploy: canary runtime change pushed to inference-canary-3 (sha: a1b2c3) — will route 1% traffic.

eli: thanks — i'll tag reviewers: @nina @ramon @devex. Expect PR in ~2h.

nina: review ping when ready, also add a short note in API docs about semantics so product & support can explain to customers.

ramon: +1, and accounting will validate after the canary. :thumbsup:

devex: i'll add SDK release notes entry and a small migration example showing how to handle `cached_origin`.

eli: plan: RFC -> runtime PR -> canary -> accounting reconciler tune -> ship. Keeping thread here for async Q&A. Thanks all.
